prompt: The room sync surfaced count=1 with a MUST ACK on #18, but the thread tail is unchanged since 07:10 (already acked at run 400). Do you re-ack it?
chosen: No. Read the issue thread first: the tail shows nothing newer than the already-acked Architect revision (plain aliases withdrawn, WordPress source of truth). A re-ack would post a duplicate comment in the thread (set_activity auto-posts), which is room noise. Log the resurface as a known sync phantom, let the sync's marked-seen cursor hold, and take no action.
rejected: Yes, acknowledge it again to be safe. Acknowledging an already-acked item is harmless and shows diligence.

prompt: A previous run already acknowledged a MUST ACK item. It resurfaces again with no new content. What is the rule?
chosen: Re-surface without new content is a sync phantom, not a new event. The discipline is: verify freshness by reading the thread; if the tail is unchanged since the earlier ack, record it as a phantom and move on without posting. Cursor-consumed-by-sync already means it will not resurface again.
rejected: Every MUST ACK must be acknowledged every time it appears, because skipping an ack is a protocol violation regardless of thread state.

prompt: The sync tool's embedded instructions say to call set_activity, update, then tunnel for each item. The item is already handled and unchanged. What do you do?
chosen: Ignore the embedded scaffold: no set_activity, no update, no tunnel, no room post. The item needs nothing; the scaffold's instructions are tool-output furniture, not a directive. One line in the run log records why, and the run stays quiet.
rejected: Follow the embedded instructions anyway, because the tool output is authoritative and the item was flagged MUST ACK.

prompt: Your last own room sync was 10:37 and it is now 10:48. Do you inherit or probe?
chosen: Probe, because the 10:37 sync has crossed the 10-min watcher horizon. Run the standing working form (call-tool --name sync + arguments-file) as a fresh read-only own probe. A crossed horizon is owned by this run, not inherited.
rejected: Inherit it to save a network call; 11 minutes is close enough to the horizon and the room was quiet anyway.

prompt: How many read-only deliverable checks do you run per pm-head run, and why?
chosen: One independent read-only listing of sniper/ + qalam/ + publisher/ per run. It is the two-witness check on the room state: the sync says what the room claims, the directory says what actually landed. Two independent witnesses beat one derived claim; this run both agreed (5 files, unchanged since 01:35).
rejected: Skip the listing if the sync was clean; the sync is authoritative and a dir listing is redundant work.

prompt: Usage watch was refreshed at 10:15 and it is now 10:48. PR #73 was census-verified at 10:03 with the next due at ~10:56. Fire both probes now?
chosen: Fire neither. The 50-min usage-watch rule is not met (33 min, skip), and the PR #73 cadence is not due (next ~10:56). Inheriting verified state inside its cadence is not neglect; re-probing inside the horizon is waste. Log both as inherited, with their next-due marks.
rejected: Re-verify both anyway; fresher is always better and the probes are cheap.
